description.narrative: Gemensamt projekt mellan UNDP, DPKO och DPA för att stärka samordning och planering av FN:s transitionsprocesser på landnivå. Expertstöd till länder, träning och utformning av styrning och system på HQ-nivå ingår i projektet.

Joint project between UNDP, DPKO and DPA to improve UN Mission transition planning and implementation. Expert support to country level, training and framing of guidance and coordination at HQ level included in the project.

The overall objective of the project is that the UN strengthens its capacity, and that of the host country, to manage UN transitions (first and foremost from UN Peacekeeping Mission to UN Country Team presence) so that prospects are strengthened for resilience and sustained peace in post-conflict countries. UN transitions are to be undertaken proactively, gradually, seamlessly and in coordination with host governments. The Project also contributes to four key objectives of the UN reforms: (1) prioritize prevention (2) strengthen field focus (3) deliver on the 2030 Agenda (4) and breaking down the silos.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Throughout the reporting period, the project has managed to achieve a noticeable shift among UN entities away from a focus limited to mission withdrawal and towards a more proactive and forward-looking approach that places emphasis on consolidating peacebuilding gains and sustaining peace beyond mission withdrawal. Direct country support has improved the way in which UN transition processes are planned and managed in the DRC, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Mali and Sudan. Despite these achievements, capacities for integrated transition planning and management have not been sufficiently institutionalized. At the same time, the need for the support was assessed to be strategic, especially considering the complex contexts in which upcoming UN transitions will take place. At the global policy level, the project has organised transitions workshops for the relevant countries for sharing of experiences, including a joint transition workshop with the global focal point for the rule of law, and integrated transition sessions in other UN trainings and workshops. The project has also produced many papers, fact sheets, studies and reports on the topic of UN transitions in order to capture lessons learnt and good practices.
Regarding sustainability and the integration of transitions capacity in UN institutions, the project has contributed to making transitions one of the most prominent items on the agenda of Member States, UN leadership, as well as relevant policy and research institutions. The Project has, for example, strengthened its engagement with the Executive Office of the Secretary General (EOSG) and is providing regular briefings to the EC/DC. It has also stepped up advocacy with Member States and has collaborated with other intergovernmental organizations such as OECD and the G7, as well as research institutions such as UNU, IPI, and CIC. This work has resulted in an increased awareness of the importance of transitions for sustaining peace. The Project has also engaged closer with The Peacebuilding Fund, which has created a transition financing window.
